2607.09600.title: Agora: Enhancing LLM Agent Reasoning Via Auction-Based Task Allocation
2607.09600.paper_summary: Enhancing the reasoning capabilities of large language model (LLM) agents requires effective orchestration of diverse expert models and tools. However, existing frameworks typically call APIs based on coarse-grained matching between tasks and the functions of expert models or tools, while overlooking critical factors such as performance variability and cost efficiency among functionally similar alternatives. To address this, we propose Agora, a framework that introduces an incentive-compatible auction mechanism for dynamically allocating tasks to expert models and tools. By treating reasoning steps as tradeable items, Agora enables agents to bid based on their rectified competence-ensuring that critical logic is routed to the most capable solver rather than the most overconfident one. Evaluations across five benchmarks show that Agora improves over matched single-model, routing, and cascade baselines under comparable candidate pools, while exposing a controllable cost-quality trade-off through a single auction parameter.
2607.09600.paper_summary_zh: 提升大型語言模型（LLM）代理的推理能力需要有效協調各種專家模型和工具。<lb/>然而，現有框架通常基於任務與專家模型或工具功能之間的粗略匹配來調用API，卻忽略了性能變異性和功能上相似的替代方案之間的成本效率等關鍵因素。<lb/>為了解決這個問題，我們提出了Agora，一個引入激勵相容拍賣機制的框架，用於動態分配任務給專家模型和工具。<lb/>通過將推理步驟視為可交易項目，Agora使代理能夠根據其修正的能力進行競標，確保關鍵邏輯被路由到最有能力的解決者，而不是最自信的解決者。<lb/>在五個基準測試中的評估顯示，Agora在可比較的候選池下優於匹配的單模型、路由和級聯基準，同時通過單一拍賣參數揭示可控的成本-質量權衡。
